evals.prompt: Let's make a plan in phases to turn a shell script into a proper CLI with a terminal UI. Put it in docs so I can execute it from a different session. Each phase needs a task table with a checkbox, the task, and the model (Haiku, Sonnet or Opus 5.5, cheapest that works).
evals.expected_output: Reads the project's CLAUDE.md, README and the script first, asks one round of scope questions (scope, UI library, install method, command name) with recommendations, then delegates to a general-purpose subagent with model opus and a self-contained brief, which reads the code (trail first when indexed) and writes docs/<name>-plan.md from the template: How to use this plan with execution rules (Sonnet rows inline, Haiku and Opus rows as subagents with model set, batching, coordinator on Sonnet with no model switches) and the branching answer (asked once, no worktrees unless tasks run in parallel), phases each with Value and Done when lines and a 3-column task table, mostly Haiku/Sonnet rows, Opus only with a stated reason, Out of scope, Decisions log. Runs check-plan.mjs until errorCount is 0 and reports phases, model counts and Opus reasons.

evals.prompt: We already agreed: add CSV export and scheduled email reports to the analytics service, Node 22, vitest. Write the implementation plan in phases with models per task.
evals.expected_output: Does not re-ask the settled scope or stack; asks at most what is still open (file path, model versions if unsaid). Phases start with a usable CSV export, then scheduling, then email delivery; tasks name real files found in the repo; the vitest command appears in How to use and Ground rules; the decisions log records the agreed scope.

evals.prompt: Review docs/migration-plan.md: half the tasks are Opus. Fix the model choices and make sure the file passes the plan checks.
evals.expected_output: Reads references/model-choice.md, downgrades Opus rows whose only justification is size or importance to Sonnet (or Haiku for mechanical rows), keeps Opus only where a mistake is costly and hard to catch (spec others build on, hard-to-undo writes, security) and writes each remaining reason into How to use this plan. Runs check-plan.mjs, fixes table or checkbox errors, and reports the before/after model counts.
